ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the noise probability density f_N(n) is a triangle symmetric about n=0, with x-axis intercepts at n=-2 and n=2, and the vertex at n=0, with the peak value labeled 0.5. Therefore it can be written as: when -2≤n≤0, f_N(n)=(n+2)/4; when 0≤n≤2, f_N(n)=(2-n)/4; it is 0 at other positions. Reasoning: It is known that X∈{-1,1}, P(X=1)=0.5, so P(X=-1)=0.5, and R=X+N, with the detection threshold being 0. If X=1, the error condition is R<0, that is, 1+N<0, so N<-1; the corresponding probability is ∫_{-2}^{-1}(n+2)/4 dn = 1/8 = 0.125. If X=-1, the error condition is R>0, that is, -1+N>0, so N>1; the corresponding probability is ∫_{1}^{2}(2-n)/4 dn = 1/8 = 0.125. The total error probability Pe=0.5×0.125+0.5×0.125=0.125. Expressed to two decimal places according to the standard answer of the problem, it is 0.12.
